title: What can you say about calcium in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 4 wordings for calcium; the strongest is "Helps build and maintain strong bones and teeth" (strong, 120-1,500 mg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Prevents or treats osteoporosis, outside FDA's authorized calcium wording".

supported_wordings.wording: Helps build and maintain strong bones and teeth.
supported_wordings.why: Listed by Health Canada and authorized in the EU after EFSA review.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 19 and older. Health Canada: 65-1,500 mg a day. EU: at least 120 mg, 15% of the 800 mg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII). ODS upper limits: 2,500 mg (19-50) and 2,000 mg (51 and older).
supported_wordings.form: Calcium from a salt on Health Canada's list (such as carbonate or citrate), counted as elemental calcium

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Prevents or treats osteoporosis, outside FDA's authorized calcium wording
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease. In the US, FDA's authorized health claim (21 CFR 101.72) has set wording and conditions (see fda_health_claims).

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Lowers blood pressure, or prevents preeclampsia
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names diseases. FDA's qualified claim on calcium and hypertension has set wording (see fda_health_claims).

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Reduces the risk of colon cancer or polyps

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
